learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what makes food safe to eat, how to identify hazards and adulteration, and the vital role of national and international food standards!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Food safety means ensuring food won't cause harm to the consumer. Food quality includes safety but also covers attributes like taste, color, texture, and nutritional value.
Hazards can be Biological (bacteria, viruses, fungi), Chemical (pesticides, cleaning agents), or Physical (glass, stones, hair) that make food unsafe to consume.
Adulteration is the intentional or accidental addition of cheaper, inferior, or harmful substances to food (like adding water to milk or brick powder to chili powder).
Governments set rules to ensure food safety. In India, FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India) regulates this. Globally, Codex Alimentarius acts as the international food code.
Industries use systems like HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) to identify and prevent food safety hazards during production rather than just checking the finished product.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Spices Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Take a glass of water and drop a spoonful of coriander (dhaniya) powder or tea leaves into it. Pure tea/coriander will float or settle slowly, while added coloring or heavy dust/brick powder will immediately streak colors into the water or sink fast!

exam_tips: 📌 Learn the full form of FSSAI and HACCP, as they are very common objective questions.
📌 Clearly distinguish between Physical, Chemical, and Biological hazards with one example for each.
📌 Remember that Codex Alimentarius translates to 'Food Code' and is recognized by the WTO for international trade.
quick_recap: ⭐ Foodborne illnesses are often caused by biological hazards like Salmonella or E. coli.
⭐ Intentional adulteration is done for financial gain, while incidental adulteration happens due to carelessness.
⭐ Implementing HACCP makes food production proactive rather than reactive.
